candidates.behaviour: A low glitch on rxd starts a frame (bit_cnt loads 10), but rxd_reg is high again at the mid-start-bit sample (prescale_reg == 0, bit_cnt == 10). The receiver abandons the frame, so bit_cnt returns to 0 and neither m_axis_tvalid nor frame_error follows.
candidates.title: rx_false_start_rejected
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline only drives well-formed frames, so the start bit is always still low at the mid-bit sample.

candidates.behaviour: A second complete, well-formed frame arrives while m_axis_tvalid is still high with m_axis_tready low. overrun_error pulses for one cycle, m_axis_tvalid stays high, and m_axis_tdata takes the second word.
candidates.title: rx_overrun_error
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline sink holds m_axis_tready high, so every word is consumed before the next one completes.

candidates.behaviour: After a word is received, m_axis_tready is held low for several cycles. m_axis_tvalid stays high and m_axis_tdata stays unchanged throughout. The word is accepted on the first cycle m_axis_tready goes high, with no overrun.
candidates.title: rx_output_backpressure_hold
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline sink never deasserts m_axis_tready, so m_axis_tvalid never waits for a handshake.

candidates.behaviour: rst is asserted while the receiver is busy mid-frame and an unread word is pending (m_axis_tvalid high). After reset, m_axis_tvalid and busy are low, and a following well-formed frame is received correctly.
candidates.title: rx_reset_during_frame_with_pending_word
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline only resets while idle, with no pending output word.

candidates.behaviour: rst is asserted while the transmitter is mid-frame with txd low (start bit or a 0 data bit). On the next clock txd returns to 1 and busy drops, and a later byte is transmitted correctly.
candidates.title: tx_reset_during_frame_returns_to_mark
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline asserts reset only while the transmitter is idle and txd is already high.

candidates.behaviour: rxd is held low for longer than two full frame times. The receiver restarts immediately after each frame error, so frame_error pulses at least twice with rxd never going high in between, and m_axis_tvalid never rises.
candidates.title: rx_break_repeated_frame_errors
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline never holds rxd low past a stop bit, and R1 needs only a single frame error.

candidates.behaviour: With prescale = 16'hFFFF, a well-formed frame carrying 8'hA5 is received. m_axis_tvalid rises with m_axis_tdata == 8'hA5, and prescale_reg reaches the full 19-bit reload value without truncation.
candidates.title: rx_receive_at_max_prescale
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline runs only at prescale 5, so the low prescale bits never toggle and the high prescale_reg bits are never used.

candidates.behaviour: With prescale = 16'hFFFF, a byte 8'h5A is accepted and transmitted. Every bit lasts prescale*8 clocks (the stop bit one clock more), prescale_reg reaches 19'h7FFF8 for the stop bit, and txd carries 8'h5A LSB first.
candidates.title: tx_transmit_at_max_prescale
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline runs only at prescale 5, so the low prescale bits and the high prescale_reg bits never toggle.

candidates.behaviour: The receiver has delivered and handed off a word (m_axis_tdata == 8'hA5, m_axis_tvalid low) and is busy receiving the next frame when rst is sampled high. On the next clock, with rst still high, busy is 0, m_axis_tvalid is 0 and m_axis_tdata is 8'h00.
candidates.title: rx_reset_clears_outputs_after_accepted_word
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline resets only while idle, never mid-frame, and never checks m_axis_tdata or busy during reset.

candidates.behaviour: rst is sampled high while the receiver's prescale_reg is above 19'd16 (mid-bit), and rxd is held low through and after reset. busy then rises on exactly the third clock after rst is released (counter value 2), and no earlier, so the new start bit is detected without waiting for the old bit timer.
candidates.title: rx_reset_mid_frame_prompt_restart
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline never resets mid-bit and never holds rxd low across a reset release.

candidates.behaviour: rst is sampled high on the same clock on which frame_error is high. On the following clock, with rst still high, frame_error is low.

candidates.title: rx_reset_on_frame_error_strobe
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline never produces a frame error, let alone resets on the pulse cycle.

candidates.behaviour: rst is sampled high on the same clock on which overrun_error is high. On the following clock, with rst still high, overrun_error is low.

candidates.title: rx_reset_on_overrun_error_strobe
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline sink is always ready, so overrun_error never pulses.

candidates.behaviour: A false start is rejected (prescale_reg == 0, bit_cnt == 10 and rxd_reg high). Exactly two clocks later busy is already 0.
candidates.title: rx_false_start_busy_release_timing
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline only sends well-formed frames, so the false-start branch never executes.

candidates.behaviour: rst is sampled high while the idle transmitter has s_axis_tready high. On the next clock, with rst still high, s_axis_tready is 0, so no transfer can be accepted during reset.
candidates.title: tx_reset_while_idle_drops_tready
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline never checks s_axis_tready while rst is high.

candidates.behaviour: rst is sampled high while the transmitter's prescale_reg is above 19'd16 (mid-bit). After release, s_axis_tready rises exactly on the second clock after rst is released (counter value 1).
candidates.title: tx_reset_mid_frame_ready_timing
candidates.why_baseline_misses: The baseline never resets the transmitter mid-bit or measures tready timing after reset.
